content: In three clinical studies, the combination of Welchol and a statin (atorvastatin, lovastatin, or simvastatin) demonstrated an additive reduction in LDL-C levels. The mean baseline LDL-C levels were 184 mg/dL in the atorvastatin study (range: 156–236 mg/dL), 171 mg/dL in the lovastatin study (range: 115–247 mg/dL), and 188 mg/dL in the simvastatin study (range: 148–352 mg/dL). The addition of 8 g of Welchol resulted in an additional 8% to 16% reduction in LDL-C levels compared to statin therapy alone. Across all three studies, the reduction in LDL-C achieved with the combination of Welchol and any dose of statin therapy was statistically superior to the reduction achieved with either Welchol or the statin alone. The effect of Welchol in combination with atorvastatin 10 mg was also evaluated. Additionally, the impact of Welchol when added to fenofibrate was assessed in 122 patients with mixed hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson Type IIb). Inclusion criteria for this study required LDL-C levels of ≥115 mg/dL and triglyceride (TG) levels between 150 mg/dL and 749 mg/dL. Patients were randomized to receive either 8 g of Welchol or placebo for six weeks in a double-blind treatment phase. The mean baseline LDL-C level at the start of randomized treatment was 144 mg/dL. The study results demonstrated that Welchol significantly reduced LDL-C, non-HDL-C, total cholesterol (TC), and ApoB levels, while significantly increasing HDL-C levels. A moderate, non-statistically significant increase in TG levels was observed compared to placebo. In another study involving patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (heFH), participants were either on a stable dose of an FDA-approved statin with LDL-C >130 mg/dL or were statin-naïve with LDL-C >160 mg/dL. This study included three phases: a single-blind placebo stabilization period, an 8-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled treatment period, and an 18-week open-label treatment period. At screening, 24% of patients were on statins, while 76% were statin-naïve. The mean baseline LDL-C level at Day 1 was approximately 199 mg/dL. A total of 186 patients completed the double-blind treatment period, and 173 patients (89%) completed 26 weeks of treatment. Welchol at 8 g/day significantly decreased plasma levels of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, TC, and ApoB, while significantly increasing HDL-C levels. Results at Week 26 were consistent with those observed at Week 8. Welchol has also been studied in the context of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, both as monotherapy and in combination with metformin, sulfonylureas, and insulin. In these studies, Welchol and placebo were administered either as three tablets twice daily with lunch and dinner or as six tablets taken with dinner alone.
